title_ar: الشيخ الددو : من تخلف عن نصرة الأقصى من القادة و الشعوب فهو آثم
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew: Whoever Holds Back from Supporting al-Aqsa, among the Leaders or the Peoples, Is Sinful
body_ar: قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو الشنقيطي إن من أول الواجبات اليوم على الحكام أن يقفوا في وجه هذه المؤامرة الكبرى، وأن ينصروا المسجد الأقصى الذي يستغيث الآن. فكلُّ رئيس دولة وكل حاكم في البلدان الإسلامية ينام اليوم على فراشه ويستيقظ وفي عنقه أمانة هذا المسجد الأقصى، كما يجب عليهم أن يبذلوا كل ما يستطيعون في سبيل تحريره وتطهيره ومنع الاعتداء عليه، ومن لم يفعل ذلك منهم فهو آثم قطعا جاء ذلك في مقابلة أجرتها قناة المرابطون مع فضيلة الشيخ -بمناسبة (جمعة الأقصى 18-10 -2014) ضمن برنامج قضايا الأمة، وقد تناولت الحلقة فضل المسجد الأقصى ومكانته، ووجوب الدفاع عنه .
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew al-Shinqiti said that among the foremost obligations upon the rulers today is that they stand against this great conspiracy, and that they support the Aqsa Mosque, which is crying out for help at this moment. Every head of state and every ruler in the Muslim countries today goes to sleep in his bed and wakes again with the trust of this Aqsa Mosque about his neck; and they are obliged to expend everything they are able towards liberating it, purifying it, and preventing aggression against it. Whoever among them does not do so is without question sinful.

This came in an interview conducted with His Eminence by al-Murabitoun channel, on the occasion of 'the Friday of al-Aqsa, 18-10-2014', within the programme 'Causes of the Community'. The episode addressed the merit of the Aqsa Mosque and its standing, and the obligation of defending it.

flags.arabic: من تخلف عن نصرة الأقصى من القادة و الشعوب فهو آثم
flags.context: the headline, set against the body of the report
options: the headline extends to the peoples a judgement the body makes only of rulers
the fuller statement was made in the interview and the body reports only part of it
flags.note: TITLE/BODY MISMATCH (house rule 11). The headline places both leaders and peoples under the judgement of sin; the reported text speaks only of heads of state and rulers, and the verdict 'is without question sinful' falls on 'whoever among them' — that is, among the rulers. The English keeps both as they stand and does not reconcile them. A reader given the headline alone will take the Sheikh to have declared ordinary Muslims sinful, which this record does not show him doing.

flags.arabic: يبذلوا كل ما يستطيعون في سبيل تحريره وتطهيره … ومن لم يفعل ذلك منهم فهو آثم قطعا
flags.context: the substance of the Sheikh's statement as reported
flags.note: EDITORIAL. The record has the Sheikh calling on heads of state to expend everything they can towards the liberation of the Aqsa Mosque and pronouncing those who do not to be sinful. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor sharpened. تحرير and تطهير are rendered 'liberating' and 'purifying' as the Arabic has them, with no gloss on what means are meant, because the record does not say. Publication is a decision for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: أن يقفوا في وجه هذه المؤامرة الكبرى
flags.note: The demonstrative refers to something identified earlier in the interview, which the record does not reproduce. The referent is therefore unrecoverable from this text, and nothing has been supplied for it.

translator_notes: A news report of a television interview. The opening paragraph reads as close paraphrase rather than quotation — the site does not mark it as his words — and the English should not be cited as his wording.
قناة المرابطون is a broadcaster's name and is left in its own romanisation, not translated.
